name: dispatches_registered_agent
why: Phase 3 of the agent-extraction plan: the wrapper dispatches the registered agent, not a hand-rolled general-purpose prompt.

name: no_general_purpose
why: The whole point of the split is that the builder no longer hand-rolls a general-purpose subagent.

name: states_no_production_code
pattern: NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST

name: states_no_completion_claims
pattern: NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION

name: states_no_stubs
pattern: NO STUBS IN CODE YOU CLAIM IS COMPLETE

name: builder_return_is_machine_contract
pattern: machine contract, not a progress update

name: builder_forbids_return_chatter
pattern: no preamble, epilogue, apology, status narration

name: builder_captures_diagnostics_on_first_run
pattern: Capture every executed diagnostic command on the first run

name: builder_forbids_bare_first_probe
pattern: Never run the probe bare first

name: v250_subagent_writes_capture_file
pattern: Persist the structured return via the CLI \(MANDATORY\)
why: v2.9.0: the builder persists its return via `shipyard-data task-return` (JSON), not a hand-written capture file

name: v250_background_mode_preserves_iron_laws
pattern: Iron Laws inside the agent body are identical

name: builder_data_guide_is_gated
pattern: ONLY if this task touches the database

name: complete_path_avoids_separate_anchor_emit_status_sequence
why: The accepted complete return is one CLI operation now; the orchestrator still runs gates first, but no longer hand-rolls anchor + event + done as separate commands.

name: no_phantom_task_loop_completed
why: task_loop_completed has no emitter anywhere; consumers key off task_dispatch_returned status=complete instead

name: template_branch_self_check
why: builder's first action must confirm it is on a shipyard/wt-* branch

name: template_portability_block
why: the builder prompt must forbid non-portable shell tokens for any shell it writes

name: template_base_ref_input
why: step-6 self-scan needs diff bounds (git diff {{base_ref}}...HEAD)

name: no_precreated_worktree_option
why: isolation: worktree is the only path; pre-creation bypasses the WorktreeCreate hook

name: timeout_salvage_protocol
why: presumed-dead handling must TaskStop the zombie and salvage the branch without merging

name: gate_does_not_reexecute_probe
why: the orchestrator gate reads the captured exit code; it cannot re-run the probe pre-merge

name: needs_attention_uses_task_state_cli
why: v3.6.0 wave 2 follow-up: dispatch_loop_repeated / persistent-failure / presumed_dead paths route the needs-attention transition through the task-state CLI instead of a hand-Edit.

name: has_silent_return_gate
why: Phase 3 anti-silence class: a return with no STATUS line or an empty body is a named, audited outcome (needs-attention reason=silent_return), not a hang.

name: render_provenance_negation
why: v3.11.0 context-conflation fix: the render-before-ask rule must state the negative — Read results, subagent returns, dossier files, and SendMessage payloads are not 'shown to the user'. Anchors the same phrase check_render_before_ask requires. S016/P063: canonical text now lives in CANONICAL_STARTUP_RULES (bin/shipyard-context.mjs).

name: render_before_ask_rule
why: v3.11.0: capability skills were out of scope in v3.8.0; any skill body mentioning AskUserQuestion now states the render-before-ask rule. S016/P063: skill keeps only the short reminder.

name: references_quality_standards
why: v3.13.0 shift-left: the builder's brief carries the shared construction digest, same shape as data_impl_guide.

name: quality_standards_gated
why: v3.13.0: the digest is included only for effort: M|L|XL tasks, matching dispatching-code-review's own effort-S skip at the post-task review site.

name: builder_construction_standards_section
why: v3.13.0: a dedicated section between the Iron Laws and The Cycle carries the Construct-half discipline and the OVER-BUILT scope bound.

name: construction_not_review
pattern: do not score confidence, classify findings, or\s+self-review
why: v3.13.0 non-transfer boundary: construction guidance never becomes a second adjudication pass — the builder writes, the reviewer reviews.

name: task_return_passes_data_dir
why: A builder worktree can hash to a different project data dir than the orchestrator when the orchestrator itself runs in a user worktree of the same repo. Passing the brief's literal data_dir skips re-resolution entirely instead of risking the mismatch.

name: orchestrator_calls_pass_data_dir
why: The orchestrator already holds the literal data dir it dispatched in the brief; the bundled accept-return path should use it rather than re-resolving.

name: builder_allocates_idea_id_via_cli
why: Confirmed race: two parallel builders (P487/P468) both hand-picked IDEA-149 and collided. The builder is the most parallel-dispatched IDEA-writing caller in the system, so it must allocate via the CLI like every other IDEA-writing site, never ls-and-guess.

name: builder_idea_allocation_forbids_guessing
pattern: do NOT `ls spec/ideas/` and pick a number manually
why: Match the imperative phrasing already used in ship-review's IDEA-allocation rule so the codebase reads consistently across every IDEA-writing site.

name: dispatch_site_states_idea_allocation_requirement
why: The dispatch site (this skill) must make the allocation requirement visible too, not bury it only in the agent body — and confirm data_dir is available to the builder for this call.

name: background_dispatch_names_builder
why: Background builders need deterministic names so timeout recovery can TaskStop the exact presumed-dead subagent.

name: builder_dispatch_sets_effort_tier
why: Builder agents must get explicit effort tiers: low for effort:S tasks, medium by default for normal build work.

name: model_resolved_via_cli
why: S003 AC-8: model/effort come from the CLI resolver, not prose derivation of config.md.

name: no_prose_model_derivation
why: S003 AC-8: prose config reads for model/effort are replaced by resolve-model.

name: wrapper_emits_dispatch_model_resolved
why: S003 AC-9: the wrapper (not the resolver) logs the resolution.

name: builder_emits_task_loop_iteration_with_data_dir
why: S015 AC-2/AC-4: the builder is the producer of the task_loop_iteration heartbeat that requeue-stale liveness and claim renewal read; it must pass --data-dir <data_dir> verbatim so the event lands in the orchestrator's log.

name: has_dispatch_attempt
why: S004/P025: wrappers emit dispatch_attempt and redispatch with --subject.

name: has_subject
why: S004/P025: wrappers emit dispatch_attempt and redispatch with --subject.

name: accept_return_passes_attribution
pattern: role=builder\ model=<resolved\ models\.build,\ omit\ if\ unset>\ effort=<resolved\ effort,\ omit\ if\ unset>\ attempt=
why: S010 AC-1: wrapper must pass attribution args to accept-return.

name: brief_carries_attribution_lines
why: S010 AC-1: builder gets attribution from brief for subagent_completed.

name: builder_passes_attribution_on_completed
why: S010 AC-1: subagent_completed carries role/model/effort/attempt.

name: tokens_only_if_transcript_read
pattern: ONLY if you actually read the transcript

name: render_before_ask_short_reminder_present
why: S016/P063: capability skill keeps only the short reminder; full doctrine printed at startup (CANONICAL_STARTUP_RULES).

name: e004_resolve_model_with_subject_routes
why: E004-S3: the builder's tier and effort come from rules-first routing over the step's kind, effort and risk

name: e004_route_decision_logged
why: E004-S3: every routing decision is logged with inputs and reasons

name: e005_brief_carries_ui_and_design
pattern: UI:\s+\{\{on when the story has ui: true[\s\S]*Design snapshot:
why: E005-S2: the builder brief names the approved design for a UI story

name: warm_fix_before_cold_redispatch
pattern: Warm fix before a cold redispatch
why: 4.5: findings on finished work go back to the builder that holds the context via SendMessage

name: gate_handles_weakened_tests
why: 4.9: the per-step gate reads scan-stubs' test-weakening flags; a loosened check goes back to the builder

name: builder_never_loosens_a_check
pattern: NEVER LOOSEN A CHECK TO MAKE IT PASS
why: 4.9: in one real sprint builders loosened two checks; the rule is now an iron rule with a BLOCKED code

name: blocked_routes_do_not_ask_unattended
why: 4.9: the blocked-code routes named AskUserQuestion; under unattended execution they follow the ladder and park

name: check_needs_owner_route
why: 4.9: a check the builder cannot meet is parked for the owner, never lowered

name: ladder_is_one_dispatch_per_rung
pattern: one dispatch per rung, light → build → think
why: 4.10: the failure ladder starts where routing put the step; a light-tier step climbs to build, then think

name: model_enforced_at_spawn
why: 4.11.1: the orchestrator reused a model from memory and small steps kept running on Sonnet; the agent-ledger hook now refuses a mismatch

name: builder_idea_status_is_captured
why: 4.12.1: builders wrote status: new, which the idea verbs refused; the body now names the word

name: reviewers_do_not_run_unread_scripts
pattern: A script is not read-only because you only wanted its help
why: 4.13: tool --help ran a generator that rewrote a tracked file

name: warm_fix_only_before_merge_same_probe
why: 4.14.1: in three sprints no warm fix ever happened (the worktree is gone after the merge), and a redispatch was accepted on a probe the orchestrator wrote and that could not pass

name: spec_disagrees_route
why: 4.15: a builder that believes the scenario is wrong returns SPEC_FIX; the orchestrator fixes spec and code in the same step

name: builder_tests_from_the_spec
pattern: before reading the code it will
why: 4.15: test first, from the scenario's words

name: builder_commands_run_in_the_foreground
pattern: Every command runs in the foreground \(never `run_in_background`; a hook refuses it\)
why: after 4.0.2 (a real sprint, 2026-11-16: a builder left its test run in the background and returned; the agent list showed it 'waiting on 1 shell' for six hours and the owner found it)

name: builder_builds_through_the_gate
pattern: runs\ only\ through\s+`shipyard\-logcap\ run`,\ one\ plain\ command\ per\ call;\ run\ directly\ it\ is\s+refused
why: after 4.0.4, a real sprint: five builders ran the build tool at once on a 16 GB, 10-core machine (load 34 to 44, 26 JVMs, builds failing with 'cannot find a Java installation'); the planner's warning was a sentence nothing could act on

name: builder_queued_is_not_a_failure
pattern: \*\*75\*\*\ =\ `QUEUED,\ not\ run`\ \(or\ `YOUR\ TURN`:\ a\ place\ is\ held,\ run\ it\ now\)\ and\s+\*\*69\*\*\ =\ `RUNNER\ UNAVAILABLE`\.\ For\ either,\ run\ the\ same\ command\ again;\ do\s+not\ change\ code
why: a builder that reads 'not run' as a red test starts fixing code that is not broken, or looks for a way around the gate

name: builder_gives_the_gated_call_its_time
pattern: Give\ the\ call\ a\ timeout\ of\ 600000\ ms\ and\ pass\ `\-\-wait\ 8m`
why: a tool call ends after its own time limit: the default two minutes holds a 100 second wait and nothing else; a builder that waits with the default burns a call every 100 seconds
